observation.visible_scene: A small multi-rotor craft (or rotor-bearing object) is held near the center of the frame against an almost black background. It has a dark oval central body with tan/golden arms radiating to spinning rotors, whose blades appear as blurred discs at the arm tips. The scene is continuous with no visible editing cut.
visible_changes: The rotor discs remain in motion blur throughout, with their blurred shapes and orientation fluctuating slightly from frame to frame, indicating the rotors keep spinning during the excerpt.

The craft's position within the frame drifts only slightly: comparing first and last views it moves a little rightward (roughly center-left to near center) while its vertical position stays about the same.
Faint background structures (a dim horizontal band and low shapes) gradually become visible along the bottom edge in the later frames, whereas the early frames show mostly uniform darkness.
The craft's overall size, shape, color and intact structure do not change across the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: The exact identity of the object and whether it is airborne, tethered, or stationary relative to the ground is not shown.
The light source and the nature of the dark surroundings (sky, interior, night terrain) are unseen.
What precedes or follows this excerpt, including any takeoff, landing, or completion of motion, is outside the crop.
uncertain_details: It is unclear whether the slight rightward shift of the craft and the emergence of bottom-edge background detail are due to object translation, camera pan/tilt, or a change in exposure/illumination; the background evidence is too dim to separate camera motion from object motion confidently.
The precise number and geometry of the rotors are obscured by motion blur.
